title.narrative: Policy and technical advice on the beneficial use of dredged materials in Colombia, including nature-based solutions

description.narrative: This project, financed through the Partners for Water Programme, focuses on policy- and technical advice for the beneficial uses of marine dredged sediments, including nature-based solutions (NbS). The core objective of the project is to provide a set of practical rules and parameters for beneficial use of dredged material. The project aligns with seven Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):• 6 (Clean water and sanitation),• 9 (Industry innovation and infrastructure),• 11 (Sustainable cities and communities),• 12 (Responsible consumption and production),• 13 (Climate action),• 14 (Life below water) and• 15 (Life on land).Activities and deliverables1. Knowledge transfer on Dutch dredging practices. Focuses on gathering and sharing insights from The Netherlands regarding licensing, operation, monitoring and approval processes for marine dredging, transferring knowledge about dredging practices in The Netherlands. Deliverable: a technical document summarising experiences and lessons learned.2. Quality requirements for sediments globally. Builds on activity 1 by analysing international practices and parameters for assessing marine dredged sediments. Deliverable: a technical document comparing global insights with lessons applicable to Colombia.3. Sediment quality analysis in Barranquilla port area. Assesses sediment quality and dredged volumes in the Port of Barranquilla, using data and methodologies from activities 1 and 2. Deliverable: a technical document evaluating sediment quality.4. Guidelines for sediment evaluation and uses. Develops procedural guidelines to assess sediment quality and potential uses, including input for updating dredging project regulations. Deliverable: a technical document outlining the guidelines, to be included in the current guidelines of INVIAS.5. Case study Barranquilla. Combines findings from activities 3 and 4 to create a case study on using marine dredged sediments for coastal protection in Barranquilla. Deliverable: documentation of the case study.6. Stakeholder engagement and capacity building. Organisation of online and in-person meetings, training sessions, workshops with stakeholders, and a closing event to present project outcomes.7. Communication and outreach. Creating project summaries, visuals, social media content, and articles to disseminate the project's findings and promote awareness.Consortium• Arcadis is the leading global natural and built asset design and consultancy firm, working in partnership with their clients to deliver exceptional and sustainable outcomes through the application of design, consultancy, engineering, project, and management services.• Fundación Herencia Ambiental Caribe (FHAC) engenders sustainable development through the use and protection of the environment and natural, cultural, and social resources, emphasising community participation processes, and strengthening identity and culture.• JESyCA is a Colombian engineering and technical consultancy firm focusing on hydrology, hydraulics and environmental engineering in river, coastal and water resources related media.• NETICS is a leading innovative research and consultancy agency in civil engineering and is internationally regarded as the expert in the field of reuse and construction with dredged material.Counterparts• The Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) – Partners for Water• The Netherlands embassy in Bogotá, Colombia• Ministerio de Transporte (Mintransporte)• Departamento Nacional de Planeación (DNP)• Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible (Minambiente).
